verdict.headline: Softer inflation cuts October hike odds, but long-term bond yields still climb to new highs
verdict.label: Close: S&P 500 7,651.54 (-0.25%), Nasdaq 26,861.06 (+0.24%), Dow 50,906.05 (-0.86%); 2Y 4.895%, 10Y ~5.30%, 30Y ~5.63%; Oct hike odds 47.1%; Brent $103.71; DXY ~101.5; gold ~$4,157; BTC ~$83,600.
verdict.rationale_short: Core PCE rose 0.2% in August and 3.0% from a year earlier, below forecasts of 0.3% and 3.3%, and October hike odds fell to about 47%. Long yields rose anyway: the ten-year closed near 5.30%, around its highest since 2007, and the thirty-year near 5.63%, about 1 basis point under its 2002 high, while the two-year barely moved. Most of the inflation miss came from a methodology revision, and the same update raised second-quarter growth to 2.2% from 1.5%; ADP's 90,000 beat added to it. The S&P 500 gave up early gains to finish down 0.25%. Micron beat and guided above consensus but slipped after hours on higher capital spending. A thirty-year close above 5.644% would confirm the move; a close under 5.44% would undo it.
verdict.lede_short: Inflation came in below forecasts and October rate-hike odds fell under 50%, yet the 10-year yield closed near its highest since 2007 and the 30-year ended about a basis point from its 2002 high. Much of the inflation miss came from a change in how prices are measured, and the same data showed faster spring growth, so long-term rates are not easing on soft prints. Friday's payrolls is the next test; a 30-year close under 5.44% would undo this read.

supporting_data.label: Core PCE rose 0.2% in August and 3.0% from a year earlier, against forecasts of 0.3% and 3.3% — but a methodology revision alone cut July's core rate from 3.3% to 3.0%, so most of the miss is measurement, not slower price growth.

The ten-year rose more than 4 basis points to 5.298% while the two-year held at 4.895% — long yields rose on a soft inflation day, so investors are demanding more to hold long bonds rather than pricing more Fed hikes.
Second-quarter GDP was revised to 2.2% annualized from 1.5%, with consumer spending at 3.8% — a stronger spring economy weakens the case that rate hikes are already slowing demand.
October hike odds fell to 47.1% on CME FedWatch, but only 10% of pricing has the Fed holding through year-end — the soft print moved the timing of the next hike, not whether it comes.

Micron reported $54.23 billion of revenue against about $50.45 billion expected and guided to $61.5 billion — the stock still slipped about 1.2% after hours as fiscal 2027 capital spending rises by more than $10 billion.
The S&P 500 fell 0.25% to 7,651.54 and the Dow 0.86% while the Nasdaq rose 0.24% — stocks gave up early gains as yields climbed, closing a September loss of 0.5% and a quarterly gain of 2%.

watchlist_mentions.note: Fiscal Q4 revenue $54.23 billion and adjusted EPS $33.42 beat; Q1 guide $61.5 billion with ~86.25% gross margin. Shares slipped about 1.2% after hours on fiscal 2027 capex rising by more than $10 billion.
Rose 1.54% to $230.71 on a day the Dow fell 0.86%, helping the Nasdaq finish higher.
Rose 1.48% to $516.50 alongside Nvidia as the Nasdaq outperformed.
Its reported price increase on AI accelerators takes effect Thursday, October 1.

trade_setups.thesis: The thirty-year rose to about 5.63% on a soft inflation day while the two-year held near 4.9%, so the long end is trading on supply, growth and inflation premium rather than the Fed path.
trade_setups.entry: Thirty-year ~5.63% against the 2002 high of 5.644% above and 5.44% below.
trade_setups.invalidation: A close above 5.644% would take long yields to levels last seen in 2001; a close under 5.44% would say the rise is fading.
trade_setups.horizon: Through Thursday's ISM and Friday's payrolls

trade_setups.thesis: Results and guidance beat by wide margins, but higher capital spending drew the after-hours focus, so the first full session decides whether demand or cost is the chip sector's story.
trade_setups.invalidation: A close above $1,066.10 would show demand outweighing the spending worry; a drop below $1,000 would make spending the issue.

trade_setups.thesis: Soft PCE cut October hike odds to 47.1%, while ADP's 90,000 beat and upward GDP revisions point the other way; payrolls decides which carries.
trade_setups.invalidation: Above 150,000 would likely push October odds back above 60%; under 50,000 would favour December.
